name: Stage Cone Optical Hierarchy 01
bounded_question: What static neutral Rest-state cone width, taper, falloff, blur and vertical scale best preserve individual Character presence and one shared dark floor across 2–5 Characters without introducing state, identity, palette, motion or product-semantic meaning?
authority_limits: Cone geometry and one-cone-per-Character remain frozen; CONE-S1 refines only optical treatment inside that carrier.
All scored Characters are Rest-state equals; no candidate may encode Opportunity, Speaking, Listening, selection, Take a Seat, rank, relationship or authority.
Human-readable Character names remain visible; CIR-S1 closed with zero survivors, so no replacement identity cue may be invented here.
Current Character colors, texture vocabulary, motion timing, right-rail content, pips, arcs, performance layout and creator-action hierarchy are excluded.
No outcome establishes production tokens, final palette, implementation values or Phase-C exit.

CREF.name: Historical Cone Interaction Reference
CREF.note: Translates the earlier qualitative prototype's Rest-like beam proportions into the neutral matrix; it is not the exact PKT-STAGE-CORE-02 pixel geometry.

CNEG.name: Broad Light Wall Negative Control
CNEG.expected_failure: hard/broad luminous wall weakens discrete Character presence and shared-floor reading

F1.name: Focused Taper
F1.risk: too narrow or fixture-like; isolated spotlight rather than inhabited presence

F3.name: Broad Shared Field
F3.risk: adjacent Characters merge or additive brightness implies relationship/state meaning

F4.name: Floor-Anchored Tall Taper
F4.risk: over-tall theatrical beam or lower-weight concentration that competes with the floor/name hinge

family_separation_law: F1 tests a narrow high-clarity taper; F2 a moderate balanced taper; F3 a broad/soft shared-field stress direction; F4 a taller lower-weight floor-anchored direction.
No candidate may differ from another by only one scalar; envelope, vertical scale, taper, blur and falloff must remain the frozen multi-parameter family definitions above.
Every Character within a family uses identical optical geometry and neutral luminance; Character identity is not encoded by beam treatment.
The fixed floor pool is identical across families so the scored variable remains the beam optical hierarchy rather than a second floor-shape experiment.

matrix.rule: All families are rendered on the same shared dark floor with the same names, Rest labels, x-centers, pool treatment and neutral field.

mechanical_floors: exactly 6 families and 4 character-count specimens per family
every scored specimen is neutral Rest state; no per-Character optical variation exists within a family
beam base remains anchored to the same shared-floor y-coordinate in every specimen
no beam or blur-expanded envelope clips the stage left/right/top bounds in normal mode
no horizontal document overflow at 320 CSS px
no authored animation, transition, texture, gradient hue or non-neutral color identity
names and REST labels remain visible and outside the beam scoring geometry
CREF and CNEG are controls and ineligible for promotion
forced-colors mode may suppress decorative beam/pool optics but must retain names, Rest labels and shared-floor structure
candidate geometry and falloff arrays exactly match the frozen method; no post-exposure mutation
subjective_falsification_after_clean_pre: FAIL if a cone reads primarily as a wall, portal, column, UI container or literal lighting fixture rather than Character presence.
FAIL if five equal Rest Characters visually collapse into one wash or produce overlap brightness that implies relationship, priority or state.
FAIL if two-Character layouts become isolated spotlights with no convincing shared-floor ensemble field.
FAIL if the beam competes with or obscures the floor/name interaction hinge.
FAIL if 320px transfer turns the cone into an unreadable sliver or dominant luminous block.
FAIL if a family needs color, texture or motion to feel volumetric and intentional.
FAIL if optical weight creates an unintended central/edge hierarchy among equal Rest Characters.
PASS means only that one static neutral optical family may proceed to a bounded incumbent Stage comparison.

result_law.promotion_scope: provisional neutral Rest-state cone optical family for later incumbent Stage comparison only

review_order: 2. five-Character wide separation and additive-overlap audit
6. forced-colors fallback confirms optics are not required for identity/state recovery
7. freeze Design Sol view before any full Stage incumbent comparison
explicit_non_authority: No full Stage successor image or pixel edit is authorized by this method freeze alone.

No state-specific intensity, Character color, texture vocabulary, motion timing, focus/selection treatment, identity cue, pip/arc meaning, rail content, Performance placement or implementation is selected.
Browser/static evidence cannot be relabeled as native Windows high-contrast, GPU, screen-reader, WACK or runtime validation.
